\section{Institutional interpolation and reduction}
\label{sec:economic-layer}

Extraction effort is a dynamical state. Market clearing determines the price that equates demand with physical supply $C=qEN$. Institutional memory is a leaky integrator of the shifted, floored softplus of the deficit (Appendix~\ref{app:memory}): a finite-window integral would introduce a second delay factor $(1-e^{-\lambda\tau_m})$ and destroy the closed-form $Z^*=\delta$.

Effort interpolates between profit-driven investment and scarcity mobilisation via $\chi\in[0,1]$. The canonical law is uniformly bounded,
\begin{equation}
\dot E=
\Bigl(1-\frac{E}{E_{\max}}\Bigr)
\Biggl[
(1-\chi)\,I_{\mathrm{profit}}(E,N)
+\chi\Biggl\{\eta E\Biggl(\frac{Z(t-\tau)}{\Delta_{\mathrm{ref}}}-\frac{E}{E_{\max}}\Biggr)
+\delta_0\frac{Z(t-\tau)}{Z_{\mathrm{ref}}+Z(t-\tau)}\Biggr\}
\Biggr],
\label{eq:effort-generalized}
\end{equation}
with bioeconomic rent \cite{gordon1954,clark1976}
\begin{equation}
I_{\mathrm{profit}}=\gamma_E\Biggl(\frac{p\,qNE-c_E E}{p_{\mathrm{ref}}\,q N_{\mathrm{ref}}E_{\mathrm{ref}}}\Biggr)_+.
\label{eq:profit}
\end{equation}
The factor $(1-E/E_{\max})$ vanishes at $E=E_{\max}$, so that face is invariant and absorbing: once $E=E_{\max}$ exactly, effort never retires. At $E=0$ the factor equals $1$; nonnegativity of $E$ comes from $F\ge 0$ when $E=0$, not from a second tangent factor. Theorem~\ref{thm:nonneg} applies for every $\chi\in[0,1]$. At $\chi=1$ this is the specialised law
\begin{equation}
\dot E=\Bigl(1-\frac{E}{E_{\max}}\Bigr)\Biggl[\eta E\Biggl(\frac{Z(t-\tau)}{\Delta_{\mathrm{ref}}}-\frac{E}{E_{\max}}\Biggr)
+\delta_0\frac{Z(t-\tau)}{Z_{\mathrm{ref}}+Z(t-\tau)}\Biggr],
\label{eq:effort-gated}
\end{equation}
which is~\eqref{eq:effort-core}. The \emph{ungated} comparison system drops the outer factor; it is used only in the table rows so labelled. The hybrid $\dot E=(\text{gated bracket})-\mu_E E$ regularises the face $E=E_{\max}$. Thresholds in Table~\ref{tab:thresholds} use $\chi=1$ and~\eqref{eq:effort-gated}. When $\chi<1$ a nonnegative bounded $I_{\mathrm{profit}}$ is an additive shift of the effort bracket: it changes $E^*$ through the same quadratic~\eqref{eq:Estar-quadratic} and therefore moves $\tau_\pm$ inside the identifiability chart of Theorem~\ref{thm:ident}, without introducing a second delay.

\section{Reduction theorems}
\label{sec:reduction-theorems}

The three- and four-state cores analysed in Sections~\ref{sec:core}--\ref{sec:four-state} are not limits of the general ledger; they are the Liebig-limiting dynamics of a single binding resource under a yield gap (Lemma~\ref{lem:liebig-gap}, Theorem~\ref{thm:weak-coupling}). The specialisation --- single stock, $S=R$, $\chi=1$, $\mu=\nu=\rho=0$, frozen-$A$ --- is a modelling choice, stated once here, not a derived limit. The theorems below characterise the finite-time decoupling error when macroeconomic feedback and waste--product feedback are small; they do not establish the cores as an asymptotic reduction of the full ledger, and the global folds of Section~\ref{sec:core} lie outside their hypotheses. The working four-state equilibrium of Section~\ref{sec:four-state} is a frozen-donor quasi-equilibrium --- not a rest point of the closed mass ledger --- and is reported as such.

Throughout, write $\mathbf x_{\mathrm{slow}}=(N,A^{\mathrm{act}},U,Z,E)$ and $\mathbf y=(K,L,A_{\mathrm{TFP}},T)$, with $p$ algebraic. Histories live in the Banach space $\mathcal C=C([-\tau,0],\mathbb R^{n_{\mathrm{slow}}})$.

\begin{definition}[Institutional-failure specialisation]
\label{def:specialisation}
The \emph{specialised system} is the general framework of Sections~\ref{sec:accounting}--\ref{sec:layers} restricted to a single resource system with a single stock--service component, $\chi=1$, the gated effort law~\eqref{eq:effort-gated}, $\mathbf C^A=\mathbf 0$, and vanishing waste-product feedback $\boldsymbol\mu=\boldsymbol\nu=\boldsymbol\rho=\mathbf 0$. Write assimilation $G(N,A)\ge 0$ and turnover $M(N,A)\ge 0$, with net increment $R:=G-M=rN(1-N/K)\,A/(A+A_0)$ (signed for $N>K$) and gross uptake $B=G=R+\kappa_A N\,A/(A+A_0)$ on $N\le K$. The single service is identified with that net increment: $S=R$ (and $S=rN(1-N/K)$ after frozen-$A$). This identification is a specialisation, not a general definition of sustainable yield. All rate coefficients of the mass ledger are nonnegative, and the immediate-waste fraction satisfies $\alpha\in[0,1]$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Exact deficit identity]
\label{lem:deficit-identity}
On every trajectory of the specialised system, and of every reduced core below,
\begin{equation}
qEN-R(N,A)=-\dot N.
\label{eq:identity-full}
\end{equation}
In the frozen-$A$ limit $A/(A+A_0)\to 1$ this is the deficit identity \eqref{eq:deficit-identity} of Section~\ref{sec:core}. Under Definition~\ref{def:specialisation} the service is identified with regeneration, so the general diagnostic \eqref{eq:liquidation-general} collapses to $\Lambda=[qEN-R]_+=[-\dot N]_+$. That collapse is a property of the specialisation, not a definition of liquidation on the unreduced ledger.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Under the institutional-failure specialisation the stock equation is $\dot N=R(N,A)-qEN$. Rearrangement is $qEN-R(N,A)=-\dot N$. The same identity holds on every reduced core whose stock equation is of that form, including the frozen-$A$ three-state system with $R$ replaced by $S$.
\end{proof}

\begin{hypothesis}
\label{hyp:scale}
There is a scale parameter $\varepsilon\in(0,1]$ such that $r_L=\varepsilon^{-1}r_{L,0}$, $\eta_A=\varepsilon^{-1}\eta_{A,0}$, $\eta_{T,0}=\varepsilon^{-1}\eta_{T00}$, $\eta_{T,1}=\varepsilon^{-1}\eta_{T10}$, and capital is written in boundary-layer form $\varepsilon\dot K=\varsigma Q-\delta_K K-\theta K\,\widetilde\Delta$, with $\varsigma\in[0,1]$ unscaled. The quantities $r_{L,0},\eta_{A,0},\eta_{T00},\eta_{T10},\varsigma,\delta_K$ are $O(1)$ and independent of $\varepsilon$.
\end{hypothesis}

\begin{hypothesis}
\label{hyp:hurwitz}
On a compact subset $\mathcal K\subset\{N,A,U,Z,E\ge 0:\,E\le E_{\max},\,N\le 2K,\,A\le A^\sharp\}$ containing the relevant equilibria and periodic orbits, the macroeconomic algebraic system $\mathbf f_{\mathrm{ODE}}(\mathbf y,\mathbf x,0)=\mathbf 0$ together with market clearing $D(p)=qEN$ admits a unique root $\mathbf y=\mathbf h(\mathbf x)$, $p=p^*(\mathbf x)$, and the Jacobian $D_{\mathbf y}\mathbf f_{\mathrm{ODE}}$ at that root is Hurwitz, uniformly in $\mathbf x\in\mathcal K$. Demand is strictly decreasing in $p$.
\end{hypothesis}

Hypothesis~\ref{hyp:hurwitz} is the standard Tikhonov spectral condition; Theorem~\ref{thm:tikhonov} is conditional on it. Uniqueness of $p^*$ is a theorem: CES demand is strictly decreasing in $p$. Uniqueness of $\mathbf h$ at frozen $(Q,\widetilde\Delta)$ follows by solving the four scalar QSS maps, which are monotone and saturate. Hurwitzness of $D_{\mathbf y}\mathbf f_{\mathrm{ODE}}$ is not a consequence of triangularity ($K,L,A_{\mathrm{TFP}}$ share $Q$) and is not proved on the whole domain. A finite-difference sweep on the literature-anchored class, $\widetilde\Delta\in[0,5]$, finds all real parts $\le-\gamma_{\mathbf y}<0$; that sweep supports the hypothesis on that class and does not replace it.

\begin{hypothesis}
\label{hyp:lipschitz}
The specialised vector field is locally Lipschitz on $\mathcal K\times\mathbf h(\mathcal K)$ away from the measure-zero floor set of the softplus, and the floor is inactive in a neighbourhood of every interior equilibrium used below (because $Z^*=\delta>0$).
\end{hypothesis}

\begin{theorem}[Exact triangular projection]
\label{thm:triangle}
Under Definition~\ref{def:specialisation}, the macroeconomic block $(K,L,A_{\mathrm{TFP}},T)$, prices, and demand do not appear in $(\dot N,\dot A,\dot U,\dot Z,\dot E)$. The ecological--institutional subsystem is therefore an exact closed projection for every $\varepsilon>0$; no singular limit is required.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Under Definition~\ref{def:specialisation} one has $C=qEN$, $\boldsymbol\mu=\boldsymbol\nu=\boldsymbol\rho=\mathbf 0$, and $\chi=1$. Then $\dot N$ depends on $(N,A,E)$ only; $\dot A$ depends on $(N,A,U)$ and the frozen or parametric $A^{\mathrm{geo}}$; $\dot U$ depends on $(N,A,U)$; $\dot Z$ depends on $(N,A,E,Z)$; and $\dot E$ depends on $(E,Z(t-\tau))$. None of these right-hand sides contains $(K,L,A_{\mathrm{TFP}},T)$, prices, or demand. The block $(N,A,U,Z,E)$ is therefore closed for every $\varepsilon>0$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Finite-time reduction to the five-state core when macroeconomic feedback remains]
\label{thm:tikhonov}
Assume the specialisation of Definition~\ref{def:specialisation} is relaxed so that a $C^1$ macroeconomic feedback of size $\varepsilon$ remains (price in effort, technology in recovery, or demand-driven extraction), and assume Hypotheses~\ref{hyp:scale}--\ref{hyp:lipschitz}. Under the strict specialisation, Theorem~\ref{thm:triangle} applies instead. Let $(\mathbf x^\varepsilon,\mathbf y^\varepsilon,p^\varepsilon)$ solve the specialised system with $\mathbf x^\varepsilon(0)$ in a compact interior subset of $\mathcal K$. Then for every finite $T>0$ there exist $\varepsilon_0,C>0$ such that for all $\varepsilon\in(0,\varepsilon_0)$,
\begin{equation}
\sup_{t\in[0,T]}\bigl\|\mathbf x^\varepsilon(t)-\mathbf x^0(t)\bigr\|
\le C(\varepsilon+\omega_A T),
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}
\bigl\|\mathbf y^\varepsilon(t)-\mathbf h(\mathbf x^\varepsilon(t))\bigr\|
\le C(\varepsilon+\omega_A T)+C\,e^{-\gamma_{\mathbf y}t/\varepsilon},
\qquad 0\le t\le T.
\end{equation}
If $\mathbf y^\varepsilon(0)=\mathbf h(\mathbf x^\varepsilon(0))+O(\varepsilon)$, the exponential is absorbed into $O(\varepsilon)$ and both suprema on $[0,T]$ are $O(\varepsilon+\omega_A T)$. If $A^{\mathrm{geo}}$ is treated as exactly frozen, the $O(\omega_A T)$ term is absent. Here $\mathbf x^0$ solves the five-state core
\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned}
\dot N&=R(N,A)-qEN,\\
\dot A&=-B(N,A)+\omega_A(A^{\mathrm{eq}}-A)+\gamma_U U,\\
\dot U&=\kappa_A N\tfrac{A}{A+A_0}-\gamma_U U,\\
\dot Z&=\tau_m^{-1}\bigl[\max\bigl(0,\mathrm{softplus}_k(qEN-R)-\tfrac{\ln 2}{k}+\delta\bigr)-Z\bigr],\\
\dot E&=\bigl(1-E/E_{\max}\bigr)\bigl[\eta E(Z(t-\tau)/\Delta_{\mathrm{ref}}-E/E_{\max})+\delta_0 Z(t-\tau)/(Z_{\mathrm{ref}}+Z(t-\tau))\bigr].
\end{aligned}
\label{eq:five-state}
\end{equation}
Here $A^{\mathrm{eq}}$ is one of the two closures of Section~\ref{sec:abiotic}. Under the dynamic derived target, $\omega_A(A^{\mathrm{eq}}-A)+\gamma_U U=\omega_A(A^{\mathrm{eq,intrinsic}}-A)+\kappa_A K$, so \eqref{eq:five-state} is the working four-state system plus the driven auxiliary $U$. Under the fixed intrinsic target it is the QSS five-state system. The delay $\tau$ enters only through the slow variable $Z$. The fast subsystem is an index-1 ODE--DAE with no delay.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Rewrite the specialised system as
\[
\varepsilon\dot{\mathbf y}=\mathbf f(\mathbf y,\mathbf x,\varepsilon),\qquad
0=\mathbf g_{\mathrm{DAE}}(p,\mathbf x),\qquad
\dot{\mathbf x}=\mathbf F(\mathbf x,\mathbf x_t,\mathbf y,p),
\]
where $\mathbf x_t(\theta)=\mathbf x(t+\theta)$, $\theta\in[-\tau,0]$. The algebraic equation has a unique solution $p=p^*(\mathbf x)$ by Hypothesis~\ref{hyp:hurwitz}. Substitute it. The fast vector field $\mathbf f(\cdot,\mathbf x,0)$ has a unique equilibrium $\mathbf y=\mathbf h(\mathbf x)$ that is uniformly asymptotically stable on $\mathcal K$, with decay rate $\gamma_{\mathbf y}>0$ independent of $\mathbf x\in\mathcal K$.

On the fast clock $s=t/\varepsilon$ the slow state $\mathbf x(\varepsilon s)$ and the delayed history $\mathbf x(\varepsilon s-\tau)$ vary at rate $O(\varepsilon)$. The delay is $O(1)$ in slow time and therefore $O(\varepsilon^{-1})$ in fast time: it is a fixed, slowly drifting parameter of the fast ODE, not a delay in the fast variables. Tikhonov's theorem for index-1 DAEs \cite{tikhonov1952,hairer1996} therefore yields
\[
\mathbf y^\varepsilon(t)=\mathbf h(\mathbf x^\varepsilon(t))+O(\varepsilon)+O\bigl(e^{-\gamma_{\mathbf y}t/\varepsilon}\bigr)
\]
after a boundary layer of width $t_\varepsilon=O(\varepsilon|\log\varepsilon|)$. The exponential is $O(\varepsilon)$ on $[t_\varepsilon,T]$, and is not $O(\varepsilon)$ at $t=0$ unless the initial datum is already $O(\varepsilon)$-close to the slow manifold. The slow variable feels the layer through the integral of the exponential: $\int_0^T e^{-\gamma_{\mathbf y}t/\varepsilon}\,dt=O(\varepsilon)$, so the induced slow error is $O(\varepsilon)$, not $O(\varepsilon|\log\varepsilon|)$. Geological freezing is controlled by cumulative donor change $\varepsilon_G(T)=G_0^{-1}\int_0^T|e_{GA}-e_{AG}+C^{A,\mathrm{lim}}|\,dt$, not by $\omega_A T$ alone: under the derived target the transfer sustaining $A^*$ is $O(1)$ as $\omega_A\to 0$. The stated bound holds in the ideal large-reservoir limit when $\varepsilon_G(T)$ is absorbed into the $O(\varepsilon)$ budget or $A^{\mathrm{geo}}$ is treated as a fixed parameter. For finite $A^{\mathrm{geo}}$ add $O(1-\sigma_{\mathrm{geo}})$. This is the ODE geometric theory of Fenichel \cite{fenichel1979} only in the fast block; no normally hyperbolic delay centre manifold is invoked.

The reduced slow vector field $\mathbf F(\mathbf x,\mathbf x_t,\mathbf h(\mathbf x),p^*(\mathbf x))$ is exactly the right-hand side of \eqref{eq:five-state}: $\boldsymbol\mu=\boldsymbol\nu=\boldsymbol\rho=\mathbf 0$ removes $W,P$ from $\dot N$ and $\dot A$, $I$ is driven by $W$ and does not feed back, and $A^{\mathrm{geo}}$ is frozen on $[0,T]$ up to an $O(\omega_A T)$ relative change that is absorbed into the $O(\varepsilon)$ budget upon shrinking $T$ or treating $A^{\mathrm{eq}}$ as a fixed parameter (Section~\ref{sec:abiotic}). Continuous dependence for retarded equations on $C([-\tau,0])$ \cite{hale1993} upgrades the $O(\varepsilon)$ vector-field perturbation to the stated $C^0([0,T])$ estimate on $\mathbf x$.
\end{proof}

\paragraph{Scope.} The argument treats the delay as a slowly drifting parameter of the fast ODE; the classical theorems \cite{tikhonov1952,fenichel1971,fenichel1979} are ODE statements, and the infinite-dimensional Fenichel-type theorems that cover slow-fast evolution systems \cite{hummelkuehn2022,kuehnsulzbach2024} apply only subject to a spectral gap and compactness of the memory kernel that are not verified here. The reduction is therefore a finite-time statement, reported as numerically verified rather than as a theorem for the delayed system; the $O(\omega_A T)$ term means the bound does not control the multi-century objects of Section~\ref{sec:four-state} on one period, a limitation also recorded in Theorem~\ref{thm:frozenA}.

\begin{theorem}[Working-core projection]
\label{thm:working-proj}
In the ideal large-reservoir limit $\sigma_{\mathrm{geo}}=1$, on the specialised system with the dynamic derived target of~\eqref{eq:aeq-derived}, write $T=\kappa_A N A/(A+A_0)$. Then
\[
\omega_A(A^{\mathrm{eq}}-A)+\gamma_U U=\omega_A(A^{\mathrm{eq,intrinsic}}-A)+\kappa_A K
\]
identically, and $(N,A,Z,E)$ satisfies the working-core equations~\eqref{eq:four-state-working} (defined in Section~\ref{sec:four-state}) exactly. The detritus $U$ is a driven auxiliary ($\dot U=T-\gamma_U U$) and does not feed back into $(N,A,Z,E)$. For finite $A^{\mathrm{geo}}$,
\[
\dot A=-B+\omega_A(A^{\mathrm{eq,intrinsic}}-A)\sigma_{\mathrm{geo}}+\kappa_A K\sigma_{\mathrm{geo}}+\gamma_U U(1-\sigma_{\mathrm{geo}})+O\bigl([{-A^{\mathrm{eq}}}]_+\bigr),
\]
so the working-core vector field is perturbed by $O(1-\sigma_{\mathrm{geo}})$ and $U$ feeds back through $\gamma_U U(1-\sigma_{\mathrm{geo}})$. Reported $\tau_\pm$ are properties of the $\sigma_{\mathrm{geo}}=1$ core.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
On the specialised system with the live derived target, $\dot A=-R-T+\omega_A(A^{\mathrm{eq}}-A)+\gamma_U U$ in the ideal large-reservoir limit. Substitute
\[
A^{\mathrm{eq}}=A^{\mathrm{eq,intrinsic}}+\frac{\kappa_A K-\gamma_U U}{\omega_A}.
\]
Then
\[
\omega_A(A^{\mathrm{eq}}-A)+\gamma_U U
=\omega_A(A^{\mathrm{eq,intrinsic}}-A)+\kappa_A K-\gamma_U U+\gamma_U U
=\omega_A(A^{\mathrm{eq,intrinsic}}-A)+\kappa_A K,
\]
which is $\omega_A(A^{\mathrm{eq,W}}-A)$ with $A^{\mathrm{eq,W}}=A^{\mathrm{eq,intrinsic}}+\kappa_A K/\omega_A$. The $U$-equation remains $\dot U=T-\gamma_U U$ and does not appear in $(\dot N,\dot A,\dot Z,\dot E)$. For $\sigma_{\mathrm{geo}}<1$ the recharge is $\omega_A[A^{\mathrm{eq}}]_+\sigma_{\mathrm{geo}}$ and the exchange remainder is $O(1-\sigma_{\mathrm{geo}})$, with an additional feedback $\gamma_U U(1-\sigma_{\mathrm{geo}})$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Detritus slaving under a fixed intrinsic target]
\label{thm:detritus}
Assume the hypotheses of Theorem~\ref{thm:tikhonov}, and hold $A^{\mathrm{eq}}=A^{\mathrm{eq,intrinsic}}$ \emph{fixed} (closure~2; not the live $D^{\mathrm{ret}}=\gamma_U U$). Write $\gamma_U=\varepsilon_U^{-1}\gamma_{U,0}$ with $\gamma_{U,0}=O(1)$ and $\varepsilon_U\to 0$. Then after a transient of length $O(\varepsilon_U|\log\varepsilon_U|)$,
\[
U(t)=U^*(N(t),A(t))+O(\varepsilon_U),\qquad
U^*(N,A)=\gamma_U^{-1}\kappa_A N\tfrac{A}{A+A_0},
\]
and $(N,A,Z,E)$ is $O(\varepsilon_U)$-close on compact time intervals to
\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned}
\dot N&=R(N,A)-qEN,\\
\dot A&=-R(N,A)+\omega_A(A^{\mathrm{eq,intrinsic}}-A),\\
\dot Z&=\tau_m^{-1}\bigl[\max\bigl(0,\mathrm{softplus}_k(qEN-R)-\tfrac{\ln 2}{k}+\delta\bigr)-Z\bigr],\\
\dot E&=\bigl(1-E/E_{\max}\bigr)\bigl[\eta E(Z_\tau/\Delta_{\mathrm{ref}}-E/E_{\max})+\delta_0 Z_\tau/(Z_{\mathrm{ref}}+Z_\tau)\bigr].
\end{aligned}
\label{eq:four-state-reduced}
\end{equation}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
With $A^{\mathrm{eq}}$ fixed at $A^{\mathrm{eq,intrinsic}}$, $\dot A=-R-T+\omega_A(A^{\mathrm{eq,intrinsic}}-A)+\gamma_U U$. The $U$-equation is linear and attracting at rate $\gamma_U$. Variation of constants gives $U=U^*+O(\varepsilon_U)$ after the transient, and $\gamma_U U^*$ cancels $T$. Continuous dependence upgrades the remainder. An interior equilibrium of~\eqref{eq:four-state-reduced} solves $qE^*=r(1-N/K)A/(A+A_0)$ and $A=A^{\mathrm{eq,intrinsic}}-qE^*N/\omega_A$ jointly. At Candidate~A the system has a positive low-$A$ equilibrium $(N^*,A^*)\approx(23.85,0.159)$. The high-stock algebraic branch gives $A^*\approx-137$, which is inadmissible. There is no large-$A$, near-logistic exploited equilibrium compatible with $N^*/K\approx 0.90$.
\end{proof}

At the Table~\ref{tab:params} baseline, $\gamma_U/r=10$, so $\varepsilon_U$ is not small: Theorem~\ref{thm:detritus} is a finite-time $O(\varepsilon_U)$ estimate and does not control global periodic orbits. The quantitative object is the working core of Theorem~\ref{thm:working-proj} and Definition~\ref{def:working-four}.

\begin{definition}[Detritus-QSS four-state core]
\label{def:qss-four}
Equation~\eqref{eq:four-state-reduced} is the QSS core under a \emph{fixed} intrinsic target. At Candidate~A it has a positive low-$A$ equilibrium $(N^*,A^*)\approx(23.85,0.159)$, outside the frozen-$A$ regime, and no high-$A$ near-logistic exploited equilibrium. It is a valid singular limit but is not dynamically connected to the high-$A$ working equilibrium used for reported $\tau_\pm$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Turnover-corrected four-state working core]
\label{def:working-four}
Equation~\eqref{eq:four-state-working} is the quantitative working core, obtained exactly by Theorem~\ref{thm:working-proj} (dynamic derived target) or by omitting $U$ with $D^{\mathrm{ret}}=0$. Here $B=R+\kappa_A N A/(A+A_0)$ and $A^{\mathrm{eq,W}}=A^{\mathrm{eq,intrinsic}}+\kappa_A K/\omega_A$ ($5050$ at baseline, $A^{\mathrm{act}*}\approx 397.87$). The four-state numerical thresholds refer to this system.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Frozen-active-pool approximation]
\label{thm:frozenA}
Let $(N,A,Z,E)$ solve either four-state core \eqref{eq:four-state-working} or \eqref{eq:four-state-reduced}, and suppose that on $[0,T]$,
\[
A(t)\ge A_{\min}>0,\qquad |\dot A(t)|\le V_A.
\]
Let $(N^{(3)},Z^{(3)},E^{(3)})$ solve the three-state core with $S(N)=rN(1-N/K)$. Then
\[
\sup_{t\in[0,T]}\bigl(|N-N^{(3)}|+|Z-Z^{(3)}|+|E-E^{(3)}|\bigr)
\le C_T\Bigl(\frac{A_0}{A_{\min}}+V_A T\Bigr).
\]
The term $V_A T$ guarantees that an initial lower bound $A(0)\ge A_{\min}+V_A T$ keeps $A(t)\ge A_{\min}$ on $[0,T]$; once that bound is assumed, the vector-field gap is $O(A_0/A_{\min})$. If $A_0/A_{\min}+V_A T=O(\eta_A)$ with $\eta_A\ll 1$, the three-state core is an $O(\eta_A)$ inner approximation on $[0,T]$, not a Tikhonov reduction.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Write $R(N,A)=rN(1-N/K)\,A/(A+A_0)$. Then
\[
R(N,A)-rN(1-N/K)=-rN(1-N/K)\frac{A_0}{A+A_0}.
\]
On $N\in[0,K]$ and $A\ge A_{\min}>0$ the right-hand side is bounded by $rK A_0/A_{\min}$. If $|\dot A|\le V_A$ on $[0,T]$, then $|A(t)-A(0)|\le V_A T$. The four-state field and the three-state field with $S(N)=rN(1-N/K)$ therefore differ, uniformly on the compact set $\mathcal K$, by a $C^0$ term of size $O(A_0/A_{\min}+V_A T)$, independently of the delay. Continuous dependence of RFDE solutions on the vector field in $C([0,T];C([-\tau,0]))$ \cite[Ch.~2]{hale1993} yields the $C^0([0,T])$ bound.
\end{proof}

At the baseline, $1/\omega_A\sim 10^3$~yr and the four-state oscillation period is $250$--$390$~yr, so $\omega_A T\not\ll 1$ on one period: Theorem~\ref{thm:frozenA} justifies the three-state core for local, near-equilibrium questions on institutional timescales of a few years (in particular the location of $\tau_-$), not for the large-amplitude cycle. That is why $\tau_-$ is essentially unchanged under restoration of $A$ (a $3.2\%$ shift, inside the approximation bound) and why the period is not.

\begin{lemma}[Soft-minimum gap]
\label{lem:liebig-gap}
Fix a service component with the $C^\infty$ soft-minimum of Section~\ref{sec:structural-production} and $w_k\ge w_{\min}>0$. If the sub-yields satisfy $\tilde Y_k\le\tilde Y_j-\Delta_y S^{\max}$ for every $j\neq k$ (a uniform gap of size $\Delta_y>0$), then the softmax weights obey
\[
\pi_j\le w_{\min}^{-1}e^{-\rho\Delta_y}\qquad(j\neq k),
\]
and therefore $\partial S/\partial\tilde Y_j=O(e^{-\rho\Delta_y})$. If each $\tilde Y_j$ is $C^1$ and Lipschitz in its own stock, $\partial S/\partial N_j=O(e^{-\rho\Delta_y})$ uniformly on that set.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Write $y_m=\tilde Y_m/S^{\max}$ and
\[
\pi_j=\frac{w_j e^{-\rho y_j}}{\sum_m w_m e^{-\rho y_m}}.
\]
Factor $e^{-\rho y_k}$ from numerator and denominator:
\[
\frac{\pi_j}{\pi_k}=\frac{w_j}{w_k}\exp\bigl(-\rho(y_j-y_k)\bigr).
\]
The gap hypothesis is $y_j-y_k\ge\Delta_y$ for $j\neq k$, and $w_k\ge w_{\min}$, $w_j\le 1$, so
\[
\pi_j=\pi_k\cdot\frac{w_j}{w_k}e^{-\rho(y_j-y_k)}\le w_{\min}^{-1}e^{-\rho\Delta_y},
\]
using $\pi_k\le 1$. Differentiating $S$ with respect to a stock that enters only $\tilde Y_j$ therefore produces a factor $\pi_j=O(e^{-\rho\Delta_y})$, uniformly on the gap set.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Decoupling at the Liebig limit]
\label{thm:weak-coupling}
Let $n$ specialised systems be coupled only through the Liebig service that enters the deficit, and optionally through a $C^1$ physical remainder of size $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{phys}}$ in regeneration or damage. Suppose that on a compact interval $[0,T]$ component $k$ maintains a uniform yield gap $\Delta_y>0$ in the sense of Lemma~\ref{lem:liebig-gap}. Set $\varepsilon_c=C e^{-\rho\Delta_y}+\varepsilon_{\mathrm{phys}}$. Then
\[
\|\mathbf X-\mathbf X^k\|_{C([0,T])}\le C_T\varepsilon_c,
\]
where $\mathbf X^k$ is the scalar four-state (respectively three-state) core of block $k$ driven by the other blocks as $O(\varepsilon_c)$ inputs. The same bound holds if the physical remainder is the only coupling and there is no gap, with $\varepsilon_c=\varepsilon_{\mathrm{phys}}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Lemma~\ref{lem:liebig-gap} makes every off-limiting service derivative $O(e^{-\rho\Delta_y})$ on $[0,T]$. Together with the physical remainder this is a $C^1$ perturbation of size $\varepsilon_c$ of the product of $n$ independent cores, restricted to the $k$-th block. Hale's continuous-dependence theorem for DDEs \cite{hale1993} gives the estimate.
\end{proof}

This is the terminal Liebig-limit phase, not a physical-decoupling hypothesis, and it does not cover the compensatory phase near yield parity (where $\Delta_y\to 0$ and the cross-derivatives are not exponentially small). Layers~2--4 and Proposition~\ref{prop:no-scalar} are the compensatory phase: a positive aggregate can still mask a deep single-component deficit. Once substitutes are exhausted or the soft-minimum has collapsed onto one factor, $\partial S/\partial N_{j\neq k}\to 0$ and the reduced core is the dynamics of that constraint. Within one resource the substitute that delays $Z$ is $A^{\mathrm{geo}}$ (mining does not enter the specialised deficit). A farmer who holds crop yield by liquidating a \emph{different} system's water, \emph{without} a yield gap, remains on the unreduced vector ledger. In the absence of a yield gap the vector system remains unreduced.

\begin{theorem}[Local Hopf persistence]
\label{thm:hopf-persist}
Assume Theorems~\ref{thm:tikhonov} and~\ref{thm:working-proj}, and assume the working four-state (respectively three-state) characteristic equation has a simple pair $\pm i\omega$ at $\tau=\tau_\star\in\{\tau_-,\tau_+\}$, with $\mathrm{d}\,\mathrm{Re}\,\lambda/\mathrm{d}\tau\neq 0$ and no other imaginary eigenvalues. Assume the fast Jacobian of Hypothesis~\ref{hyp:hurwitz} remains uniformly Hurwitz at the joint equilibrium, and that mass-accumulation compartments that do not feed back ($\mu=\nu=\rho=0$) stay outside the delay loop. Under the strict specialisation of Theorem~\ref{thm:triangle} the core spectrum is a literal factor of the full characteristic function, so the Hopf points persist exactly (the downstream block remaining Hurwitz). If a residual macroeconomic feedback of size $\varepsilon$ is restored, there exists $\varepsilon_0>0$ such that the specialised system in the ideal large-reservoir limit has a Hopf point $\tau_\star(\varepsilon)=\tau_\star+O(\varepsilon)$. For the saturated finite-reservoir ledger the shift is $\tau_\star(\varepsilon,\sigma_{\mathrm{geo}})=\tau_\star+O(\varepsilon)+O(1-\sigma_{\mathrm{geo}})$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The joint equilibrium $(\mathbf x^*,\mathbf h(\mathbf x^*))$ of the specialised system exists for small $\varepsilon$ by the implicit function theorem: the slow equilibrium conditions are independent of $\mathbf y$ once $p=p^*(\mathbf x)$ and $\mathbf y=\mathbf h(\mathbf x)$ (the core equilibrium does not use $Q$), and $D_{\mathbf y}\mathbf f$ is invertible by Hypothesis~\ref{hyp:hurwitz}. The linearised specialised system at this equilibrium is a DDE in the slow variables coupled to a Hurwitz ODE in the fast variables, with delay only in $(Z,E)$. The characteristic function is
\[
\det\bigl(\lambda I-J_{\mathrm{slow}}(\lambda,\tau)-B_{\mathrm{sf}}(\lambda I-J_{\mathrm{fast}})^{-1}B_{\mathrm{fs}}\bigr)=0,
\]
where $J_{\mathrm{slow}}(\lambda,\tau)$ is the core quasi-polynomial symbol. The Schur complement is $O(\|B_{\mathrm{sf}}\|\,\|B_{\mathrm{fs}}\|/\mathrm{dist}(\lambda,\sigma(J_{\mathrm{fast}})))$. On a neighbourhood of $\pm i\omega$ the fast resolvent is $O(1)$, and the fast-slow blocks $B_{\mathrm{sf}},B_{\mathrm{fs}}$ are $O(\varepsilon)$ after the Tikhonov scaling (macro rates sit in $J_{\mathrm{fast}}$, not in the coupling once $\mathbf y$ is eliminated at leading order; residual coupling through $Q(\mathbf y)$ into $\widetilde\Delta$ is $O(\varepsilon)$ on the slow clock). Rouch\'e's theorem therefore perturbs the simple imaginary roots by $O(\varepsilon)$. Transversality $\mathrm{d}\,\mathrm{Re}\,\lambda/\mathrm{d}\tau\neq 0$ persists, so the crossing remains a Hopf bifurcation \cite{hale1993,diekmann1995,faria1995}.
\end{proof}

Theorems~\ref{thm:tikhonov}--\ref{thm:hopf-persist} are the one-system claim, on finite time and conditional on Hypothesis~\ref{hyp:hurwitz}; the global events of Numerical Result~\ref{thm:two-folds} are outside their hypotheses. The object delivered by the general framework in the institutional-failure regime, for one resource, is the five-state core; the quantitative working model is the dynamic-target projection of Theorem~\ref{thm:working-proj}; the three-state core is the inner approximation of that working model on institutional timescales; the local Hopf points of the working core persist in the specialised system. Theorem~\ref{thm:tikhonov} transfers local Hopf points; the global events of Numerical Result~\ref{thm:two-folds} are properties of the named inner DDE.

\begin{theorem}[Forward invariance of the mass orthant]
\label{thm:nonneg}
Assume the sign restrictions of Definition~\ref{def:specialisation} and the gated law~\eqref{eq:effort-gated}. On the specialised system and on the five-, four-, and three-state cores, the set
\[
\Omega=\bigl\{N,A^{\mathrm{act}},U,P,W,I,A^{\mathrm{geo}},Z\ge 0,\; 0\le E\le E_{\max}\bigr\}
\]
is forward invariant. In particular $A^{\mathrm{geo}}$ cannot become negative. The bound $E\le E_{\max}$ holds for~\eqref{eq:effort-generalized} and fails for the ungated comparison system (table rows so labelled). The stoichiometric core of Section~\ref{sec:unified-core} uses a signed memory and is outside the scope of the $Z\ge 0$ statement.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
At $N=0$, $R=B_{\mathrm{turn}}=qEN=0$, so $\dot N=0$. At $A^{\mathrm{act}}=0$, $B=e_{AG}=0$ and the remaining terms of \eqref{eq:abiotic} are nonnegative. At $A^{\mathrm{geo}}=0$, $e_{GA}=C^{A,\mathrm{lim}}=0$ and $\dot A^{\mathrm{geo}}=e_{AG}\ge 0$. The clamp $[A^{\mathrm{eq}}]_+$ keeps $e_{GA}\ge 0$ if the derived target is transiently negative. At $U=0$, $\dot U=\kappa_A N A/(A+A_0)\ge 0$. At $P=0$ and $W=0$ every source is a nonnegative routing of a nonnegative flux. At $Z=0$ the floored source is nonnegative, so $\dot Z\ge 0$. At $E=0$ the gated effort law gives $\dot E\ge 0$; at $E=E_{\max}$ the prefactor vanishes and $\dot E=0$ (weakly invariant). Nagumo's condition holds on each face.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Waste--product feedback as a regular perturbation]
\label{thm:waste}
Let $\mathbf x^0$ solve the five-state core, and let $\mathbf x^{\varepsilon_w}$ solve the specialised system with $\|\boldsymbol\mu\|,\|\boldsymbol\nu\|,\|\boldsymbol\rho\|\le\varepsilon_w$ (operator norms on $\mathcal K$). Then on every finite $[0,T]$,
\[
\|\mathbf x^{\varepsilon_w}-\mathbf x^0\|_{C([0,T])}\le C_T\varepsilon_w.
\]
If the feedback is not small, $W$ (respectively $P$) is an additional slow state and the reduced system is the five-state core plus that compartment. The coefficient $\nu$ routes durable product back to $N$; it is not a recovery technology. Recovery $\rho$ is routed to $A^{\mathrm{act}}$. Specialisation sets both to zero.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The compartments $W$ and $P$ satisfy linear equations with $O(1)$ sources (routed extraction) and strictly negative diagonal decay. On any finite $[0,T]$ they remain bounded, uniformly in the driving five-state trajectory on the compact set $\mathcal K$. The feedback terms $-N\mu W$ in $\dot N$ and $\chi^{\mathrm{rec}}\rho W$ in $\dot A$ are therefore $C^1$ and of size $O(\varepsilon_w)$ on $\mathcal K\times[0,T]$. The resulting vector field is an $O(\varepsilon_w)$ $C^1$ perturbation of the five-state DDE. Continuous dependence \cite[Ch.~2]{hale1993} yields the $C^0([0,T])$ estimate. If $\varepsilon_w$ is not small, $W$ or $P$ is retained as an additional slow state by definition of the reduced system.
\end{proof}
When that extra slow state is retained the Hopf cubic of Theorem~\ref{thm:hopf-cubic-complete} is no longer a complete local spectrum: $W$ (or $P$) enlarges the quasi-polynomial. Reported $\tau_\pm$ are the $\varepsilon_w=0$ specialisation.

\begin{theorem}[Sampled-data monodromy]
\label{thm:sampled}
Linearise the effort-bounded three-state core about the interior equilibrium and replace delayed feedback by sample-and-hold of period $T_r$: $E$ is constant on each $((k-1)T_r,kT_r]$ and is updated at $t_k=kT_r$ by one Euler step of the effort law,
\[
y(t_k^+)=y(t_k^-)+T_r\bigl(C_E y(t_k^-)+C_Z z(t_k^-)\bigr).
\]
Between reviews the variational system is the ODE
\begin{equation}
\frac{d}{dt}\begin{pmatrix}x\\z\\y\end{pmatrix}
=
\begin{pmatrix}A_N&0&A_E\\ B_N&-1/\tau_m&B_E\\ 0&0&0\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}x\\z\\y\end{pmatrix}
=:A_{\mathrm{hold}}\,
\begin{pmatrix}x\\z\\y\end{pmatrix}.
\label{eq:hold}
\end{equation}
The monodromy of one review interval is
\begin{equation}
M(T_r)=
\begin{pmatrix}1&0&0\\0&1&0\\0&T_r C_Z&1+T_r C_E\end{pmatrix}
\exp(A_{\mathrm{hold}}T_r).
\label{eq:monodromy}
\end{equation}
The sampled equilibrium is exponentially stable if and only if every eigenvalue of $M(T_r)$ satisfies $|\lambda|<1$. A Neimark--Sacker (sampled Hopf) crossing occurs at those $T_r$ for which $M(T_r)$ has a simple pair $e^{\pm i\theta}$, $\theta\notin\{0,\pi\}$, and the remaining spectrum inside the open disc. As $T_r\to 0$,
\[
\frac{M(T_r)-I}{T_r}\to
\begin{pmatrix}A_N&0&A_E\\ B_N&-1/\tau_m&B_E\\ 0&C_Z&C_E\end{pmatrix},
\]
the Jacobian of the continuous $\tau=0$ core, so the sampled system recovers the continuous undelayed linearisation. The statement is about this sample-and-hold/Euler review scheme, not about the continuous-delay DDE.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
On each open interval $((k-1)T_r,kT_r]$ the effort perturbation $y$ is held constant, so the variational equation of \eqref{eq:stock-core}--\eqref{eq:Z-core} at frozen $E$ is $\dot\xi=A_{\mathrm{hold}}\xi$ with the displayed $A_{\mathrm{hold}}$. The solution operator over one hold interval is $\exp(A_{\mathrm{hold}}T_r)$. The review map is one explicit Euler step of the effort law, $y\mapsto y+T_r(C_E y+C_Z z)$, which in $(x,z,y)$ coordinates is left-multiplication by the shear matrix in~\eqref{eq:monodromy}. The monodromy of the periodic linear system is the composition $M(T_r)$. Exponential stability of the sampled equilibrium is equivalent to $\rho(M(T_r))<1$ \cite[Ch.~8]{hale1993}. For the singular limit,
\[
\exp(A_{\mathrm{hold}}T_r)=I+A_{\mathrm{hold}}T_r+O(T_r^2),
\]
and left-multiplication by $I+T_r E_{\mathrm{jump}}+O(T_r^2)$ produces
\[
\frac{M(T_r)-I}{T_r}\to
\begin{pmatrix}A_N&0&A_E\\ B_N&-1/\tau_m&B_E\\ 0&C_Z&C_E\end{pmatrix},
\]
the Jacobian of the continuous undelayed core.
\end{proof}

Figure~\ref{fig:monodromy} is the spectral radius of this $M(T_r)$ for gated Candidate~A. Annual review is unstable on that core because the undelayed linearisation is already unstable. A Neimark--Sacker pair restabilises the sampled equilibrium at $T_r^{\mathrm{NS}}=47.536$~yr; a period-doubling multiplier $-1$ occurs at $T_r^{(-1)}=79.143$~yr. The $T_r\approx 3$--$4$~yr (anchovy) and $6$--$12$~yr (sprat) windows of Section~\ref{sec:empirical} are zeros of the stage-structured review map, a different operator. Both statements are $\det\bigl(M-e^{i\theta}I\bigr)=0$ on the map to which they refer, not a separate mechanism.

\begin{theorem}[Dimensionless identifiability]
\label{thm:ident}
Effort $E$ is dimensionless, as is $E_{\max}$; $Z$, $\delta$, and $Z_{\mathrm{ref}}$ share the units of the filtered deficit, so $Z_{\mathrm{ref}}/\delta$ is dimensionless. Let $e=E/E_{\max}$, $n=N/K$, and
\[
\varrho=\frac{qE_{\max}}{r},\qquad
a=\frac{\delta}{\Delta_{\mathrm{ref}}},\qquad
b=\frac{\delta_0\delta}{\eta E_{\max}(Z_{\mathrm{ref}}+\delta)}.
\]
At an interior equilibrium of the three-state gated core,
\[
e^*=\frac{a+\sqrt{a^2+4b}}{2},\qquad
\frac{N^*}{K}=1-\varrho e^*.
\]
Write $\lambda_F=rK/\Delta_{\mathrm{ref}}$ for the flow-scale group (Candidate~A has $\lambda_F=2$). After scaling time by $r^{-1}$, the local Hopf delays $r\tau_\pm$ depend on
\[
\varrho,\quad \lambda_F,\quad a,\quad b,\quad \frac{Z_{\mathrm{ref}}}{\delta},\quad \frac{\eta}{r},\quad r\tau_m
\]
and on $\operatorname{sp}_k'(0)=1/2$. The group $\lambda_F$ enters because the softplus argument is $qEN-S(N)$, not $(qEN-S(N))/\Delta_{\mathrm{ref}}$, unless one sets $\Delta_{\mathrm{ref}}=rK$. In particular the four combinations $(qE^*,E^*/E_{\max},\eta E^*/\Delta_{\mathrm{ref}},\delta_0/\eta)$ do \emph{not} determine $H$: $A_E=-qN^*$ still contains $q$ separately unless $E$ is scaled by $E_{\max}$ as here. Candidates~A and~B are two points in $(\eta/r,\varrho)$, not one class.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
At an interior rest $qE^*N^*=S(N^*)$, so the softplus argument vanishes and $Z^*=\delta$. The effort equilibrium~\eqref{eq:Estar-quadratic} divided by $\eta E_{\max}$ is
\[
-\,e^2+\frac{\delta}{\Delta_{\mathrm{ref}}}e+\frac{\delta_0\delta}{\eta E_{\max}(Z_{\mathrm{ref}}+\delta)}=0,
\]
i.e.\ $e^2-ae-b=0$ with the displayed $a,b$. The unique positive root is $e^*=\bigl(a+\sqrt{a^2+4b}\bigr)/2$. Then $N^*/K=1-qE^*/r=1-\varrho e^*$. After the time change $s=rt$, one has $A_N/r=1-2n^*-\varrho e^*$, $A_E$ scales into the coordinate $e$, $B_N$ and $B_E$ scale by $r\tau_m$ and the factor $\mathrm{sp}_k'(0)=1/2$, $C_E/r$ depends on $(\eta/r,e^*,a,b)$, and $C_Z/r$ depends on $(\eta/r,e^*,Z_{\mathrm{ref}}/\delta,b)$. The cubic $H$ is homogeneous of degree six in these entries, so its positive roots $\omega^2/r^2$ and the dimensionless delays $r\tau_{n,k}$ are functions of the listed groups only. The combination $(qE^*,e^*,\eta E^*/\Delta_{\mathrm{ref}},\delta_0/\eta)$ does not determine $A_E=-qN^*$ unless $E$ is scaled by $E_{\max}$.
\end{proof}

\begin{numresult}[Lower boundary of the inner three-state problem]
\label{thm:two-folds}
For the effort-bounded three-state core at Candidate~A the lower bistable boundary is the disappearance of the stable large cycle at a fold of periodic orbits in $\tau\in[5.574,5.576]$ (amplitude $25.0$ at $\tau=5.574$; adaptive-mesh collocation with variational Floquet tracking resolves the dominant multiplier as a single real eigenvalue --- imaginary part identically zero at every measured point --- rising monotonically from $0.240$ at $\tau=4.0$ to $0.964$ at $\tau=5.5815$ with orbit residual $\sim10^{-12}$; the signature of a real $+1$ crossing, i.e. a saddle-node of periodic orbits, not a complex pair). The small unstable branch born at the subcritical Hopf $\tau_-=3.666$ undergoes a continuation-supported fold at $\tau\approx 5.587$ (real multiplier $1.0514$ at $\tau=5.584$ to $0.99898$ at $\tau=5.587$; Fourier collocation succeeds through $\tau=5.58667$, residual $5\times 10^{-14}$, amplitude $21.80$, period $313.76$~yr, and fails at $\tau=5.590$). The two families do not meet (amplitudes $\approx 25$ and $\approx 21.7$; periods $\approx 322.9$ and $\approx 314.3$~yr). The $\sqrt{\tau-\tau_{\mathrm{SNPO}}}$ collision scaling of a single SNPO therefore does not apply (rigorous instances of saddle-node bifurcations of periodic orbits in DDEs exist for specific classes \cite{beretka2020}, but this boundary is not one). The upper-window attractor is a period-1 limit cycle. Fourier collocation pins two distinct families through the table value $\tau_{\mathrm{fold,R}}=148.3$ (Appendix~\ref{app:methods}, Figure~\ref{fig:upper-families}): the Hopf small branch, residual $\sim 10^{-13}$ on $\tau\in[130,150.30]$, amplitude $0.11$--$1.87$; and an interior large family, residual $\sim 10^{-13}$ on $\tau\in[147.5,160]$, amplitude $15.9$--$19.5$, $E_{\max}\le 26$. Those families remain distinct at $\tau=148.3$. A third family with $E\ge E_{\max}$ collocates down to $\tau\approx 144.5$. On that large cycle at $\tau=5.55$ the filter floor never binds, $E\le 9.2\ll E_{\max}$, and $N\ge 68.7$: the termination is not a gate singularity, not a graze of $N=0$, and not a homoclinic connection to the interior equilibrium (the period is $324$~yr and decreasing). The variational collocation resolves the dominant multiplier as real throughout (imaginary part zero), so the earlier complex-pair interpretation from shooting is superseded: the fold is a saddle-node of periodic orbits (real $+1$ crossing), not a Neimark--Sacker or torus. The orbit remains a converged fixed point of the collocation map through $\tau=5.5815$ (residual $\sim10^{-12}$), while long-horizon simulation shows the basin collapse between $\tau=5.574$ and $5.576$; the exact crossing point and the $0.002$~yr gap remain to be pinned. These are classifications of the inner three-state DDE, not of the gated four-state working model.
\end{numresult}

\begin{numresult}[Working four-state Hopf pair]
\label{thm:four-hopf}
The characteristic matrix $\Delta(\lambda)=\lambda I-A_0-A_\tau e^{-\lambda\tau}$ of the gated working core \eqref{eq:four-state-working} at the frozen-donor equilibrium $(N,A^{\mathrm{act}},Z,E)=(89.52562,397.8665,\ln 2/10,2.08962)$ has simple imaginary roots at
\[
\tau_-=3.78487~\mathrm{yr}\quad(\text{period }250.44~\mathrm{yr}),\qquad
\tau_+=150.12175~\mathrm{yr}\quad(\text{period }159.13~\mathrm{yr}),
\]
with $|\det\Delta(i\omega,\tau)|<10^{-18}$. These are the pair of Table~\ref{tab:thresholds}. Fourier collocation produces a small periodic orbit of residual $\sim 10^{-13}$ immediately below $\tau_+$ (amplitude $0.090$ at $\tau=150.082$).
\end{numresult}

\begin{numresult}[Gated four-state working-core fold locations]
\label{thm:four-folds}
Carry continuation of the large-amplitude cycle of the gated working core \eqref{eq:four-state-working} (Candidate~A; converged orbit state and delay history carried between steps, $10^4$--$10^5$~yr per step) locates the two global folds at
\[
\tau_{\mathrm{term,L}}^{(4)}\approx 5.63~\mathrm{yr},\qquad
\tau_{\mathrm{fold,R}}^{(4)}\approx 64.4~\mathrm{yr}.
\]
The lower fold brackets the disappearance of the large cycle (steady at $\tau=5.62$, peak-to-peak $N$-amplitude $\approx 23$; collapsed by $\tau=5.64$); the upper fold brackets its reappearance on the low-$\tau$ side (steady at $\tau=64.5$, amplitude $\approx 11$; collapsed by $\tau=64.25$). The resulting topology is a narrow lower bistable window $(3.78,5.63)$~yr, a wide monostable interval $(5.63,64.4)$~yr, and a wide upper bistable window $(64.4,150.1)$~yr in which the large cycle coexists with the stable equilibrium but, from generic far-from-equilibrium histories, is reached only for $\tau$ above roughly $75$--$100$~yr (depleted-stock histories only near $\tau\gtrsim135$). Cycle periods run from $\approx 371$~yr at $\tau=4.5$ to $\approx 320$~yr at the lower fold, and from $\approx 156$~yr near $\tau_+$ to $\approx 73$~yr at the upper fold. Whether either fold is a saddle-node of periodic orbits (versus a Neimark--Sacker or torus-mediated transition) is not established by these runs; the inner problem's lower boundary is a tight pair of folds rather than a single SNPO (Numerical Result~\ref{thm:two-folds}).
\end{numresult}

\paragraph{Status of the four-state folds.} Conjecture~1 of earlier drafts is resolved as follows: the fold \emph{locations} of the gated working core are now computed (Numerical Result~\ref{thm:four-folds}). The four-state upper fold ($\approx 64.4$~yr) differs from the three-state value ($\approx 148.3$~yr) by more than a factor of two: the linearised Hopf pair transfers within a few percent, but the upper global event does not --- the shared linearisation does not carry the nonlinear diagram. The qualitative five-regime topology matches the inner problem (wide monostable interval flanked by two bistable windows), but the windows are wider. The classification of the folds (fold of periodic orbits vs Neimark--Sacker/torus) and persistence in the full augmented system over infinite time remain open.

The hybrid law $\dot E=\text{(gated bracket)}-\mu_E E$ renders the face $E=E_{\max}$ strictly inward and removes a monodromy degeneracy of the gated vector field. Thresholds in Table~\ref{tab:thresholds} use~\eqref{eq:effort-gated}.

The first Lyapunov coefficient at a Hopf of \eqref{eq:char} is the Hassard--Faria--Magalhães cubic \cite{faria1995,hassard1981,guckenheimer1983}, evaluated from the exact second and third derivatives of \eqref{eq:stock-core}--\eqref{eq:effort-core} at equilibrium (Appendix~\ref{app:methods}). Under unit Hermitian normalisation of the right eigenvector and $q^*\Delta'(i\omega)p=1$,
\[
l_1(\tau_-)=+5.75\times 10^{-5},\qquad l_1(\tau_+)=+3.55\times 10^{-4}
\]
for gated Candidate~A: both crossings are subcritical. The small unstable orbit of Numerical Result~\ref{thm:two-folds} exists for $\tau>\tau_-$ and satisfies $\|N-N^*\|\sim C\sqrt{\tau-\tau_-}$. Ungated Candidate~B has $l_1(\tau_-)=-9.84\times 10^{-5}$ (supercritical; no lower fold) and $l_1(\tau_+)=+2.19\times 10^{-3}$, in agreement with Table~\ref{tab:thresholds}.

\section{Reduced core and bifurcation structure}
\label{sec:core}

\subsection{Governing equations}
For a dominant stock with logistic yield $S(N)=rN(1-N/K)$,
\begin{align}
\dot N &= S(N)-qEN, \label{eq:stock-core}\\
\dot Z &= \frac{1}{\tau_m}\Bigl[\max\Bigl(0,\;\mathrm{softplus}_k(qEN-S(N))-\tfrac{\ln 2}{k}+\delta\Bigr)-Z\Bigr], \label{eq:Z-core}\\
\dot E &= \Bigl(1-\frac{E}{E_{\max}}\Bigr)\Biggl[\eta E\Biggl(\frac{Z(t-\tau)}{\Delta_{\mathrm{ref}}}-\frac{E}{E_{\max}}\Biggr)+\delta_0\frac{Z(t-\tau)}{Z_{\mathrm{ref}}+Z(t-\tau)}\Biggr].
\label{eq:effort-core}
\end{align}
The factor $(1-E/E_{\max})$ enforces $E\in[0,E_{\max}]$ by construction. Extraction $qEN\to 0$ as $N\to 0$, so $N\ge 0$ is forward invariant. The identity
\begin{equation}
qEN-S(N)=-\dot N
\label{eq:deficit-identity}
\end{equation}
is exact on the specialised three-state core, where $S$ is the frozen-$A$ regeneration. Liquidation on that core is $\Lambda(t)=\max(0,-\dot N)$, which is \eqref{eq:liquidation-general} after the identification $S=R$. The delay $\tau$ is the time between observing that signal and mobilising effort. The filter time $\tau_m$ is an ordinary relaxation constant, not a second delay.

\subsection{Closed-form equilibrium}

At any interior equilibrium $qE^*N^*=S(N^*)$, the softplus argument vanishes, the floor is inactive, and
\begin{equation}
Z^*=\delta,
\end{equation}
independent of $\tau_m$, of $k$, and of $(N^*,E^*)$. Substituting into $\dot E=0$ (away from $E=E_{\max}$) produces the quadratic
\begin{equation}
-\frac{\eta}{E_{\max}}(E^*)^2+\eta\frac{Z^*}{\Delta_{\mathrm{ref}}}E^*+\delta_0\frac{Z^*}{Z_{\mathrm{ref}}+Z^*}=0,
\label{eq:Estar-quadratic}
\end{equation}
with a unique positive root. The stock then follows
\begin{equation}
N^*=K\bigl(1-qE^*/r\bigr),
\label{eq:Nstar}
\end{equation}
which is positive if and only if $qE^*<r$. Direct substitution of $(N^*,Z^*,E^*)$ into \eqref{eq:stock-core}--\eqref{eq:effort-core} gives residuals at machine precision. For Candidate~A ($\eta=0.914$, $E_{\max}=30$, $\delta_0=0.01$, $\Delta_{\mathrm{ref}}=1$, $\tau_m=5$~yr, $k=10$, $\delta=\ln 2/10$, $r=0.02$, $K=100$, $q=0.001$) one has
\[
N^*\approx 89.55,\qquad E^*\approx 2.090,\qquad Z^*\approx 0.0693.
\]
At $N=0$ the same algebra gives $Z\to\delta$ and $E\to E^*$: institutional memory sustains baseline effort against zero yield, but $qE^*\cdot 0=0$, so the extinction boundary does no physical harm. Linearisation in $N$ at that boundary is $\dot n=(r-qE^*)n$. The survival condition $r>qE^*$ is identical to $N^*>0$. Interior and extinction equilibria therefore exchange stability at a transcritical bifurcation $r=qE^*$ and cannot be simultaneously stable.

\subsection{Characteristic equation and the Hopf cubic}

Linearising about the interior equilibrium with $x=N-N^*$, $z=Z-Z^*$, $y=E-E^*$ gives
\[
\dot x=A_N x+A_E y,\qquad
\dot z=B_N x+B_E y-\tau_m^{-1}z,\qquad
\dot y=C_E y+C_Z z(t-\tau),
\]
with $A_N=r(1-2N^*/K)-qE^*$, $A_E=-qN^*$, $B_N=(qE^*-S'(N^*))/(2\tau_m)$, $B_E=qN^*/(2\tau_m)$, and $C_E,C_Z$ the effort-law coefficients at equilibrium (the gate $(1-E/E_{\max})$ contributes only to $C_E$). The characteristic quasi-polynomial is the single-delay cubic
\begin{equation}
\det\begin{pmatrix}\lambda-A_N&0&-A_E\\-B_N&\lambda+\tau_m^{-1}&-B_E\\0&-C_Z e^{-\lambda\tau}&\lambda-C_E\end{pmatrix}=0.
\label{eq:char}
\end{equation}
Writing $d=1/\tau_m$, $P(\lambda)=(\lambda-A_N)(\lambda+d)(\lambda-C_E)$ and $L(\lambda)=B_E(\lambda-A_N)+A_E B_N$, this is the identity $P(\lambda)=C_Z L(\lambda)e^{-\lambda\tau}$. For a Hopf root $\lambda=i\omega$, $\omega>0$, the modulus condition is the real cubic in $x=\omega^2$
\begin{equation}
\boxed{\;H(x)=(x+A_N^2)(x+d^2)(x+C_E^2)-C_Z^2\bigl[B_E^2 x+(A_E B_N-A_N B_E)^2\bigr]=0.\;}
\label{eq:hopf-cubic}
\end{equation}
\begin{theorem}[Complete local Hopf spectrum]
\label{thm:hopf-cubic-complete}
For the three-state gated core, $\lambda=i\omega$ with $\omega>0$ is a characteristic root if and only if $x=\omega^2$ is a positive root of $H$ and
\[
\tau=\bigl(-\arg(P(i\omega)/(C_Z L(i\omega)))+2\pi k\bigr)/\omega,
\qquad k\in\mathbb Z,\;\tau>0.
\]
A cubic has at most three positive roots, so there are at most three Hopf-frequency families.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The characteristic determinant expands to the identity $P(\lambda)=C_Z L(\lambda)e^{-\lambda\tau}$, with
\[
P(\lambda)=(\lambda-A_N)(\lambda+d)(\lambda-C_E),\qquad
L(\lambda)=B_E(\lambda-A_N)+A_E B_N.
\]
Set $\lambda=i\omega$, $\omega>0$. Taking moduli and using $|e^{-i\omega\tau}|=1$ gives $|P(i\omega)|=|C_Z|\,|L(i\omega)|$. Squaring both sides,
\[
|i\omega-A_N|^2\,|i\omega+d|^2\,|i\omega-C_E|^2
=C_Z^2\bigl(|B_E|^2\omega^2+(A_E B_N-A_N B_E)^2\bigr),
\]
which is $H(\omega^2)=0$ after the substitutions $|i\omega-A_N|^2=\omega^2+A_N^2$ and likewise for $d$ and $C_E$. Conversely, any positive root $x=\omega^2$ of $H$ yields a complex number $P(i\omega)/(C_Z L(i\omega))$ of modulus one, hence of the form $e^{-i\omega\tau}$ for
\[
\tau=\frac{-\arg\bigl(P(i\omega)/(C_Z L(i\omega))\bigr)+2\pi k}{\omega},\qquad k\in\mathbb Z,
\]
and the values with $\tau>0$ are Hopf delays. A real cubic has at most three positive roots, so there are at most three frequency families.
\end{proof}

For both Candidate~A and Candidate~B, $H$ has exactly two positive roots. Sweeping $\eta\in[0.5,3.0]$ yields zero or two positive roots throughout --- never one or three. The local Hopf spectrum is therefore complete: two frequency families, with higher branches at $\tau_{n,0}+2\pi k/\omega_n$.

\paragraph{Why roots come in even pairs.} From the linearisation (Appendix~\ref{app:linear}), $B_N=-(1/2\tau_m)A_N$ and $B_E=-(1/2\tau_m)A_E$ (the deficit signal is $qEN-S(N)=-A_Nx-A_Ey$ and $\operatorname{sp}_k'(0)=1/2$), so the cross term vanishes identically, $A_EB_N-A_NB_E\equiv 0$, and the cubic reduces to $H(x)=(x+A_N^2)(x+d^2)(x+C_E^2)-C_Z^2B_E^2x$. Since $H(0)=A_N^2d^2C_E^2>0$ and $H(x)\to+\infty$, the positive roots occur in even number (zero or two), never one or three --- the algebraic reason the $\eta$-sweep finds no singleton.

\begin{numresult}[Interval Newton on the Hopf cubic]
\label{thm:interval-hopf}
Write $H$ for the monic cubic~\eqref{eq:hopf-cubic} with coefficients from Appendix~\ref{app:linear}. Interval Newton starting at each floating-point positive root produces a unique simple enclosure ($0\in H(X)$, $0\notin H'(X)$) of width at most $4\times 10^{-17}$ in $x=\omega^2$. The argument formula of Theorem~\ref{thm:hopf-cubic-complete} then encloses the fundamental delays. Gated Candidate~A:
\[
\tau_-\in[3.6661490142739,\,3.6661490142743],\qquad
\tau_+\in[150.3584773101408,\,150.3584773101421].
\]
Ungated Candidate~B:
\[
\tau_-\in[6.2135987340180,\,6.2135987340183],\qquad
\tau_+\in[76.2906356879512,\,76.2906356879518].
\]
Gated Candidate~B is $\tau_-\in[5.5128407314433,\,5.5128407314436]$, $\tau_+\in[80.4245267142270,\,80.4245267142276]$. This certifies the local spectrum of~$H$. It is not an interval certificate of any global fold.
\end{numresult}

\subsection{Bifurcation diagram}

A Hopf bifurcation is local: it cannot annihilate a pre-existing large-amplitude cycle. The global disappearance of that cycle is located by pseudo-arclength continuation of the orbit itself, integrated for $10^4$--$10^5$ periods per step, not by fixed-initial-condition bisection (which mislocates folds by $>20$~yr under the critical slowing down near each Hopf \cite{scheffer2009,carpenter2011}).

The topology of the inner three-state DDE, and of the ungated four-state DDE, is the same five-regime sequence with the lower large-cycle event as in Table~\ref{tab:thresholds}. Those numbers are continuation-supported for the named DDE. They are not an approximation of the gated four-state working model. The gated inner large-cycle termination is a finite-period, finite-amplitude fold of the large-amplitude orbit whose dominant Floquet multiplier is real and approaches $+1$ (adaptive-mesh collocation with variational Floquet tracking: imaginary part identically zero, $0.240$ at $\tau=4.0$ to $0.964$ at $\tau=5.5815$; Numerical Result~\ref{thm:two-folds}) --- the signature of a saddle-node of periodic orbits, not a Neimark--Sacker or torus event. It is not a homoclinic connection and not a gate singularity. Because the small-amplitude unstable branch folds separately at $\tau\approx 5.587$, the lower boundary is a pair of nearby folds of two different periodic-orbit families, so the $\sqrt{\tau-\tau_{\mathrm{SNPO}}}$ collision scaling of a single saddle-node does not apply. (Appendix~\ref{app:methods}, Figures~\ref{fig:bifurcation}--\ref{fig:cycle}).

\begin{enumerate}
\item $0<\tau<\tau_-$ (Undelayed Panic Instability): equilibrium unstable; a single large-amplitude cycle is the attractor.
\item $\tau_-<\tau<\tau_{\mathrm{term,L}}$: equilibrium a stable focus; the large cycle coexists (lower bistable window, $\approx 0.5$--$2$~yr wide).
\item $\tau_{\mathrm{term,L}}<\tau<\tau_{\mathrm{fold,R}}$ (Phase-Stabilised Delay Window): monostable settling; the equilibrium is the sole attractor.
\item $\tau_{\mathrm{fold,R}}<\tau<\tau_+$: the large cycle reappears beside the still-stable equilibrium (upper bistable window, $\approx 1$--$2$~yr wide).
\item $\tau>\tau_+$ (Delay-Overshoot Instability): equilibrium unstable; the cycle is the sole attractor.
\end{enumerate}

The lower Hopf of the effort-bounded inner core at Candidate~A is subcritical ($l_1(\tau_-)=+5.75\times 10^{-5}$). The upper crossing is subcritical as well ($l_1(\tau_+)=+3.55\times 10^{-4}$), matching the large cycle immediately below $\tau_+$. The lower window is a large-cycle termination plus a continuation-supported small-branch fold (Numerical Result~\ref{thm:two-folds}), not a single SNPO. The upper-window attractor is a collocation-pinned period-1 cycle; $148.3$ is not a meeting of the Hopf small branch with that family (Figure~\ref{fig:upper-families}). Reported $\tau_\pm$ are the four-state gated values in Table~\ref{tab:thresholds}.

\paragraph{Basin capture.}
Inside either bistable window \cite{scheffer2003}, histories sitting at a \emph{large} stock with low effort are captured by the cycle; near-collapse histories recover to the quiet equilibrium. Abundance plus slow (or, in the lower window, still-short) adjustment is the exposed trajectory, not scarcity.

\paragraph{Robustness.}
Within the parameter subregion where the Candidate~A two-Hopf pair exists, one-at-a-time variation across the reported ranges preserves that pair and the lower-boundary structure of Numerical Result~\ref{thm:two-folds}. Outside the bounded $r$-window the system becomes delay-independently stable or lacks a positive equilibrium. Candidate~B has a supercritical lower Hopf and no lower fold. The gated four-state folds are not reported. The pair $(\tau_-,\tau_+)$ exists only for $r$ in a bounded window: approximately $(0.008,0.022)$~yr$^{-1}$ at Candidate~A's effort response, extending to $\approx 0.061$~yr$^{-1}$ at $\eta=3$. The literature range $r\in[0.005,0.4]$ in Table~\ref{tab:params} is wider than this instability window; outside the window the cores are delay-independently stable or have no positive equilibrium. $\tau_-$ itself lies in $3.7$--$7$~yr across the two effort laws and both candidates, and in $4$--$25$~yr across the full $(r,\eta)$ rectangle --- inside the documented distribution of environmental-governance lags \cite{hocherman2025}. $\tau_+$ is primarily controlled by the biological time $1/r$, but also depends on the effort-response chart: Candidates~A and~B share $r=0.02$ and have $\tau_+\approx 150$ and $\tau_+\approx 76$~yr respectively.

\subsection{Two liquidation channels}
\label{sec:two-channel}

The single-channel core treats all excess extraction as culling standing stock. Write $B_{\mathrm{birth}}(N)$ for births, not the abiotic uptake of Section~\ref{sec:abiotic}. Split net regeneration as $B_{\mathrm{birth}}(N)=S(N)+\kappa r N$, $M(N)=\kappa r N$, and split extraction by $\psi\in[0,1]$:
\[
C_{\mathrm{stock}}=\psi\,qEN,\qquad C_{\mathrm{recruit}}=(1-\psi)\,qEN.
\]
The extended stock equation
\begin{equation}
\dot N=\max\bigl(0,\,B_{\mathrm{birth}}(N)-C_{\mathrm{recruit}}\bigr)-M(N)-C_{\mathrm{stock}}
\label{eq:two-channel-stock}
\end{equation}
is non-negativity-preserving for every $\psi$: at $N=0$ every term vanishes. Away from the recruitment floor, \eqref{eq:two-channel-stock} reduces identically to $\dot N=S(N)-qEN$. The floor never binds at the interior equilibrium (the binding condition reduces to $-\psi S(N)>\kappa r N$, which is impossible). Hence $(N^*,Z^*,E^*)$, the Jacobian, the characteristic equation, and both Hopf points are independent of $\psi$ and $\kappa$.

The folds are global and feel the floor. Continuation gives $\tau_{\mathrm{fold,R}}(\psi{=}1)\approx 132.00$~yr and $\tau_{\mathrm{fold,R}}(\psi{=}0)\approx 132.50$~yr: a $0.4\%$ shift, within continuation tolerance of the single-channel value. All thresholds of Table~\ref{tab:thresholds} are computed at $\psi=1$; the channel mix leaves the Hopf points exactly unchanged and shifts the folds by $\lesssim0.5\%$, so the table is representative across the channel spectrum, while trough depths (below) are channel-dependent. Large-amplitude troughs differ substantially. At $\tau=115$~yr (Candidate~A, $\kappa=0.5$), a long-lived transient reaches $N\approx 33$ under pure culling and $N\approx 10$ under pure recruitment suppression. Stock-culling removes reproducing biomass and brakes decline immediately; recruitment suppression leaves the standing stock to background mortality. Under fixed excess demand $D=0.7>S_{\max}=0.5$, culling hits $N=0$ at $t\approx 158$; recruitment suppression approaches zero asymptotically ($t\approx 430$ to $N<1$).

\label{tab:psi-assignment}
